lead.headline: Morgan Stanley's staked ETP launch marks institutional yield-seeking in crypto as Dwelly's $170M AI rollup round signals infrastructure repricing
lead.tldr: Traditional finance is moving from passive crypto exposure to active yield extraction, while infrastructure capital chases AI-rollup convergence at $170M checks—suggesting the market is repricing what 'infrastructure' means.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week the boundary between traditional finance and crypto yield collapsed on one side while AI and rollup infrastructure fused on the other, so we are tracking where capital is actually landing versus where it is merely parking.

top_signals.title: AI rollup startup Dwelly raises $170m backed by EQT and General Catalyst
top_signals.summary: AI rollup startup Dwelly has raised $170 million in funding. The round was backed by major investors EQT and General Catalyst, with participation from prominent AI founders.
top_signals.why_it_matters: A $170M AI rollup round from EQT and General Catalyst indicates infrastructure investors are underwriting convergence plays between AI compute and blockchain settlement, repricing the entire infrastructure stack away from generic L1s toward application-specific execution layers.

top_signals.title: Morgan Stanley Launches Ether and Solana ETPs with Staking
top_signals.summary: Morgan Stanley Investment Management has expanded its digital asset offerings by launching Ether and Solana exchange-traded products (ETPs). Notably, these products include staking capabilities, marking a significant move by a major traditional financial institution into yield-generating crypto assets.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Morgan Stanley's staked Ether and Solana ETPs represent the first major TradFi entry into yield-generating crypto native mechanics, which will force competitors to match staking yields and likely compress fee structures across the ETP landscape.

top_signals.title: Crypto hacks hit record high in H1 2026 as losses top $1 billion, Blockaid says
top_signals.summary: Crypto hacks reached a record high in the first half of 2026, with total losses exceeding $1 billion. Ethereum and Solana projects were the most targeted, losing $332 million and $326 million respectively.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Record H1 2026 hack losses exceeding $1 billion, with Ethereum and Solana nearly tied as top targets, means investors must now underwrite security risk as a systematic protocol-level variable rather than an operational afterthought.

top_signals.title: Strategy Raises $544.5M and Buys Back STRC Shares
top_signals.summary: MicroStrategy has increased its US dollar reserves to $3.75 billion by raising $544.5 million through stock sales. The company also executed a $25 million buyback of STRC shares.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Strategy's $544.5M raise alongside a $25M share buyback signals Saylor is treating the equity as a volatility product with embedded BTC optionality, which reprices how the market should value the company's treasury strategy versus its software business.

top_signals.title: Coldcard Likely 4th Attack Wave Sweeps Nearly 389 BTC: Galaxy
top_signals.summary: Galaxy's Alex Thorn has identified a suspected fourth wave of attacks targeting Coldcard users. The breach reportedly impacted 462 addresses, resulting in the loss of approximately 388.93 BTC.
top_signals.why_it_matters: A fourth suspected Coldcard attack wave netting 389 BTC demonstrates hardware wallet supply chain security is a recurring failure mode that institutional custody providers can monetize through insurance and attestation products.

top_signals.title: Strategy posts $8.2 billion loss as bitcoin holdings increase 11% during Q2
top_signals.summary: Strategy reported a significant loss of $8.2 billion in the second quarter, driven by a decline in Bitcoin prices compared to the previous year. Despite the financial loss, the company increased its total Bitcoin holdings by 11% during the period.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Strategy's $8.2B Q2 loss on 11% higher BTC holdings proves the accounting mismatch between mark-to-market impairment and conviction-driven accumulation is now a feature of public-market crypto exposure, not a bug.

deals.summary: AI rollup startup Dwelly has raised $170 million in funding. The round was backed by major investors EQT and General Catalyst, with participation from prominent AI founders.
MicroStrategy has increased its US dollar reserves to $3.75 billion by raising $544.5 million through stock sales. The company also executed a $25 million buyback of STRC shares.
Digital Currency Group has officially acquired the cryptocurrency exchange Luno. DCG had previously provided seed funding to the platform back in 2014.
Payward, the parent company of Kraken, has acquired the wallet business from Magic Labs. This move aims to enhance Kraken's self-custody and onboarding capabilities for users.

Circle has acquired IBM's extensive blockchain patent portfolio, consisting of over 680 patent families and nearly 1,000 issued patents. This acquisition positions Circle as the largest holder of blockchain patents in the United States.

on_the_radar.title: World Cup generated $20B in blockchain prediction market volume: Chainalysis24m
on_the_radar.summary: Chainalysis reports that the World Cup drove $20 billion in trading volume across blockchain-based prediction markets. This highlights a significant surge in the adoption of decentralized betting and forecasting tools during major global sporting events.

on_the_radar.title: Aviva Investors launches tokenized fund after Central Bank of Ireland approval21m
on_the_radar.summary: Aviva Investors has launched a tokenized fund following regulatory approval from the Central Bank of Ireland. This move represents a significant step in bringing traditional institutional asset management onto the blockchain.

on_the_radar.title: Ostium blames off-chain breach for $24 million exploit, rules out smart contract flaw
on_the_radar.summary: Ostium has reported a $24 million exploit resulting from an off-chain breach rather than a smart contract vulnerability. The team stated that trader collateral remains safe and a recovery plan for liquidity providers is forthcoming.

on_the_radar.title: Binance launches regulated gold, silver options through ADGM exchange12m
on_the_radar.summary: Binance has launched regulated gold and silver options trading through its exchange in the Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM). This move integrates traditional precious metals with digital trading infrastructure under a regulated framework.

on_the_radar.title: BNY to bring transfer agency records onchain in blockchain push11m, BNY to bring transfer agency records onchain in blockchain pushBNY is launching a blockchain-based transfer agency platform as the bank expands its digital asset infrastructure and moves core financial records onchain.
on_the_radar.summary: BNY is launching a blockchain-based transfer agency platform to move core financial records onchain. This initiative is part of the bank's broader strategy to expand its digital asset infrastructure.

on_the_radar.title: South Korea Plans Crypto Law as Tax Repeal Reaches Committee
on_the_radar.summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission (FSC) is planning a comprehensive cryptocurrency law to regulate stablecoins and exchanges. Simultaneously, lawmakers are reviewing the repeal of a proposed 22% crypto tax originally scheduled for 2027.

on_the_radar.title: Tether signs tokenization deal with Nairobi Securities Exchange28m, Tether signs tokenization deal with Nairobi Securities ExchangeThe agreement covers tokenized securities, blockchain-based market infrastructure and the potential use of USDT as a settlement layer.
on_the_radar.summary: Tether has entered a strategic partnership with the Nairobi Securities Exchange to implement tokenized securities and blockchain-based market infrastructure. The deal also explores the integration of USDT as a settlement layer for the exchange.

on_the_radar.title: European Institutions Launch RL1 Blockchain Network
on_the_radar.summary: Ten European financial institutions have established RL1, a blockchain cooperative designed for regulated markets. The network focuses specifically on the tokenization of assets to improve efficiency within the financial sector.

on_the_radar.title: Kraken opens Jersey Mike’s IPO to retail investors through tokenized shares and direct allocations24m
on_the_radar.summary: Kraken is enabling retail investors to participate in the Jersey Mike's IPO via tokenized shares and direct allocations. This move represents a significant application of real-world asset (RWA) tokenization to democratize access to traditional equity markets.

on_the_radar.title: Core Scientific ties its AI pivot to AMD in multi-gigawatt infrastructure deal
on_the_radar.summary: Core Scientific has entered a strategic partnership with AMD to develop AI data-center capacity in the U.S. The deal starts with 500 MW of capacity available from 2027 and can scale up to 2.5 GW, including stock warrants for AMD.

on_the_radar.title: The SEC's Warning to a $25.9 Billion Market: Why Risk Curators Are in the Crosshairs
on_the_radar.summary: SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce has warned that on-chain vaults and lending strategies may be subject to existing securities laws. This signal targets a market valued at approximately $25.9 billion, potentially increasing regulatory pressure on risk curators.

on_the_radar.title: Ethereum And Solana Lead H1 2026 Crypto Hack Losses
on_the_radar.summary: Ethereum and Solana experienced the highest volume of crypto losses in the first half of 2026. According to Blockaid, these losses were primarily driven by protocol exploits and compromised private keys.

worth_a_read.note: SEC vault guidance and institutional DeFi framing will shape how regulated entities custody and deploy on-chain assets in the next compliance cycle.

worth_a_read.title: Will Robinhood Chain Succeed Where Coinbase’s Base Stumbled?
worth_a_read.note: Robinhood Chain versus Base comparison offers a testable framework for evaluating whether distribution or developer tooling wins in L2 market share.

worth_a_read.title: How One Share in Seoul Broke Hyperliquid’s Largest Equity Market
worth_a_read.note: The Seoul equity market breaking Hyperliquid's largest position provides a concrete case study in perp-AMM liquidity risk during correlated spot squeezes.

worth_a_read.title: Charts of the Week: Solana Sweeteners
worth_a_read.note: Solana incentive structures are being measured against Ethereum's post-Dencun economics, with direct implications for validator revenue and stake concentration.

worth_a_read.title: Open Letters, Open Weights, Openly Divided: AI Giants Stake Out Positions
worth_a_read.note: AI giants' open-weight positioning divides reveal how compute moats and data licensing are being underwritten differently across the major labs, with downstream effects on decentralized AI plays.

linkedin_post:
Morgan Stanley is now collecting Solana staking yield in a wrapper your compliance officer can sign off on. That is not adoption. That is extraction infrastructure finally meeting institutional standards.

We have watched ETPs accumulate BTC and ETH for years. The staked variant changes the underwriting. Yield is no longer something DeFi native; it is a line item in a TradFi product sheet. Competitors will match. Fee compression follows. The question is who captures the spread between on-chain yield and wrapper fees.

Same week, Dwelly pulls $170M from EQT and General Catalyst for an AI rollup. Infrastructure capital is not waiting for L1 valuations to recover. It is chasing execution layers that bundle compute and settlement. The category is being redefined in real time.

The test: if staking ETPs see inflows while native DeFi yields compress, the value shifts to wrapper providers and away from protocol treasuries. If Dwelly's rollups actually absorb AI inference demand, the infrastructure stack reprices again. Both are underwritable. Neither is certain.

We are watching the fee split.
